name: Text Generation Inference
notable_features: Rust server plus a router for multi-model deployments
Optimized architectures for modern models out of the box, with best-effort AutoModel fallback for everything else
On-the-fly quantization with bitsandbytes, EETQ and fp8, plus 4-bit NF4/FP4 from bitsandbytes
Container targets for AMD, Gaudi, Intel and llama.cpp/TRT-LLM variants, and a SageMaker entrypoint
Was the default HF-hosted serving path and is still the reference most HF Inference Endpoints docs describe
hardware_caveats: ARCHIVED BY THE OWNER AND READ-ONLY. The GitHub API reports archived: true with the last push on 2026-03-21 and the final release v3.3.7 published 2025-12-19. It accepts no development, so it is a dead end for anything new. Note the archived flag and the README's 'maintenance mode' notice together mean both facts: the repo is read-only, and the project's own stated policy was already maintenance-only (minor bug fixes, documentation, lightweight tasks) before archiving

NOT MERGED INTO vLLM - a widely repeated misconception. What was donated downstream is the pattern of optimised transformers model architectures that downstream engines reuse; the codebase itself was not absorbed. See notes for the README's exact wording
Still in production at Hugging Face, powering Hugging Chat and the Inference API/Endpoints, so 'deprecated' here means retired by maintainers, not unused in the world
Its quantization feature matrix predates the current generation of engines; what worked here may not reflect present-day kernels
Backend variety (AMD, Gaudi, Intel, SageMaker) existed mostly as Dockerfiles, with uneven depth behind each - a pattern that contributed to the maintenance burden
best_for: Reading how a production HF serving stack was put together, as a historical reference
Existing deployments that have not yet migrated off it
avoid_for: Any new deployment - it is archived and unmaintained
Anything needing current model architectures or current quantization kernels
New feature work of any kind
notes: Status deprecated and confidence deliberately moderate: the repo is ARCHIVED and read-only (archived flag true, last push 2026-03-21, final release v3.3.7 on 2025-12-19), so most capability claims are historical rather than current. CORRECTION TO A COMMON MISCONCEPTION, verified against the README on 2026-10-04: TGI was NOT merged into vLLM. It was retired. The README's own words are 'text-generation-inference is now in maintenance mode. Going forward, we will accept pull requests for minor bug fixes, documentation improvements and lightweight maintenance tasks', followed by an explanation that 'TGI has initiated the movement for optimized inference engines to rely on a transformers model architectures. This approach is now adopted by downstream inference engines, which we contribute to and recommend using going forward: vLLM, SGLang, as well as local engines with inter-compatibility such as llama.cpp or MLX.' The architectural idea - optimised transformers model architectures shared with downstream engines - was donated rather than the codebase. So there is no TGI code inside vLLM; there is a design pattern and a recommended migration path. A reader who believes TGI was absorbed should correct that here. Recorded because TGI was a significant GPU serving engine and its retirement is itself a fact worth having in the knowledge base; recommended migration targets are vLLM or SGLang. Confirmed still in use at Hugging Face to power Hugging Chat and the Inference API/Endpoints, which is the useful nuance behind the deprecation: retired upstream by maintainers, still deployed in production at Hugging Face.
